name: Fairmont Hotel Macdonald
positioning: A Châteauesque railway hotel from 1915 on a bluff above the North Saskatchewan River in downtown Edmonton
best_for: Travelers who want a historic hotel with river valley views in downtown Edmonton
Guests who want Fairmont Gold with private check-in and evening canapes

facts.text: The hotel was designed in the Châteauesque style by the Montreal firm Ross and MacFarlane.
The hotel is named for Sir John A. Macdonald, Canada's first prime minister.
The hotel sits on a bluff above the North Saskatchewan River in downtown Edmonton.
A glass-sided funicular drops from the hotel's area straight onto the river valley trails.
The Art Gallery of Alberta and Royal Alberta Museum are a 10-minute walk from the hotel.
The Harvest Room serves breakfast, lunch and dinner with river views and a menu built on Alberta beef, wild game, Ocean Wise seafood and herbs from the hotel's own garden.
The Confederation Lounge makes cocktails with the hotel's own honey and homemade bitters.
Weekend afternoon tea is offered, with signature sandwiches, delicate pastries and loose-leaf teas.
Sunday brunch is a buffet held in the Empire Ballroom, with live cooking stations.
The health club has two floors, with a saltwater pool, whirlpool, outdoor sun deck and squash court.
Fairmont Gold rooms have private check-in and concierge on the 7th floor, deluxe continental breakfast and evening canapes.

highlights.text: The hotel sits on a bluff above the North Saskatchewan River in downtown Edmonton.
A glass-sided funicular drops from the hotel's area straight onto the river valley trails.
The Queen Elizabeth II Suite is a bi-level suite with a large foyer, a service pantry and a dining and living area for hosting private dinners.
The Confederation Lounge makes cocktails with the hotel's own honey and homemade bitters.

considerations.text: Hallway noise can carry into rooms, depending on how booked the hotel is; light sleepers should bring ear plugs.
Some city-facing rooms have a single narrow window, so the room can feel dim.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the upscale positioning.
